n tagged `source: \"api\"`\n* **Manage a server's accounts** — complete OAuth yourself (e.g. the SDK's\n `runOAuthLogin`, or you
r CI's own sign-in) and upload the token to a named\n account; list, rename, choose the default, and delete accounts. Tokens are\
n write-only: no route returns one\n* **Run a headless agent turn** — send a message history, get back the\n assistant reply, th
e platform operations it invoked, references to any\n resources it created (eval suites), and token usage; the model is pinned\n
server-side and billed to the project\n* **Send feedback** — report a bug, a missing capability, or something\n confusing to the

MCPJam team at the moment you hit it; the same endpoint the
 `send_feedback` MCP tool calls

All endpoints operate on servers
you have already added to a project in the\nhosted inspector. Managing API keys remains UI-only — see\n[Not in the API yet](#not-

in-the-api-yet).

## Base URL

```text theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1
```

The API is p

ath-versioned. All routes on this page are relative to the base
URL above.

## Authentication

Every request needs an MCPJam

API key in the `Authorization` header:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -X POST \
 "https://app.mcpjam.com
/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/tools\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY\" \\\n -H \"Content-Type

: application/json" \
 -d '{}'
```

### Creating a key

1. Open [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings

/api-keys)
 in the hosted app (the card at the top of this page takes you there
 directly).
2. Click **Create API key**, na
me it, and pick the **organization** it will act in.\n3. Copy the key (`sk_…`) immediately — **it is shown exactly once** and neve

r
 stored by MCPJam in retrievable form.

Keys can be revoked from the same page at any time. Revocation takes effect
immedi

ately.

### Scope

A key is bound to one MCPJam organization at creation and acts **as you,
inside that organization**. Per-r
equest authorization still applies: a call\nonly succeeds if the key's owner can access that project and server. A key\ncan never

reach projects outside its organization.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Two deliberate restrictions while in preview:
>
> * **API keys canno
t manage API keys.** Requests to the key-management surface\n> with an `sk_…` bearer fail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. Create and revok

e keys in
> the UI.
> * **Guest sessions cannot use the API.** Sign in to create keys.

### Keep keys secret

Treat an API

key like a password:

* Load it from an environment variable or secret manager — never commit it to
 source control or ship i
t in client-side code.\n* Scope keys narrowly: one key per integration, named so you can tell them apart.\n* Rotate by creating a
replacement key, switching traffic, then revoking the old one.\n* If a key leaks, revoke it immediately in\n [**Settings → API ke
ys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).\n\nIf you see `401 UNAUTHORIZED` with `details.reason: \"ORPHANED_KEY\"`, the key
\nis no longer bound to an organization and cannot be used — create a new key\nfrom [Settings](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api

-keys).

## Conventions

**Requests.** Operations on servers are `POST` with a JSON body (most accept
an empty `{}`). **Reads
** — the catalog listings and eval-run polling — are\n`GET` and take their options (`cursor`, `limit`, filters) as query\nparamete

rs.

**Responses.** Three envelope shapes, used consistently:

| Kind | Shape |
| - | - |
| Single resource | The resource o
bject directly |\n| Collection | `{ \"items\": [...], \"nextCursor\": \"...\" }` — `nextCursor` omitted on the last page |\n| Erro
r | `{ \"code\": \"...\", \"message\": \"...\", \"details\": {...} }` with a matching HTTP status |\n\n**Pagination.** Collections
are cursor-based. Pass the previous response's\n`nextCursor` as `cursor` in the next request (body field on `POST` lists,\nquery
parameter on `GET` lists). Cursors are opaque — don't parse them.\n\n**Authoring vs running suites.** `POST /eval-suites` creates
a runnable suite\n(the suite plus its test cases) **synchronously** and responds `201` with the\n`suiteId`, WITHOUT running anythi
ng — author once, run later. `POST /eval-runs`\nis the async counterpart: it validates and creates a run synchronously, then\ndeta
ches execution and responds `202` with a `runId`. Poll\n`GET /eval-runs/{runId}` until `status` is `completed`, `failed`,\n`cancel

led`, or `timed_out`.

**IDs.** Every identifier the API takes is discoverable through the API
itself: `GET /projects` lists yo
ur projects, `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers`\nlists each project's servers, and `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites`\nlists

its eval suites. Start from `GET /me` to confirm which account a key
acts as.

## Errors

Errors always use the canonical bo
dy `{ code, message, details? }`. The `code`\nis stable and machine-readable; `message` is human-readable and may change;\n`detail

s` is an optional, unstructured bag.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | Missing, invalid, revok
ed, or orphaned key |\n| `OAUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | The **target MCP server** needs an OAuth grant — distinct from a bad key |\n| `A
UTH_REQUIRED` | 403 | The **target MCP server** allowed the connection and asked for sign-in on this call. `details.authChallenge`
carries the parsed challenge. Your key is fine — see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-in-challenges) |\n| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Key is va
lid but not allowed to do this — or the **target MCP server** rejected the credentials MCPJam presented (retrying with a different
MCPJam key will not help; reconnect or re-authorize the server) |\n| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | Malformed body or parameters |\n|
`NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown project, server, or resource |\n| `CONFLICT` | 409 | The resource isn't in a state that accepts this
write — a stale `expectedRevision`, a duplicate name, or an environment that can't currently be launched. Re-read and retry |\n| `
FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` | 422 | The target server doesn't support this MCP capability |\n| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests
— see [Rate limits](#rate-limits) |\n| `SERVER_UNREACHABLE` | 502 | Could not connect to the target MCP server |\n| `TIMEOUT` | 5

04 | The target MCP server connected but didn't respond in time |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Something failed on our side |

Ne
w error codes may be **added** over time; treat unknown codes as\nnon-retryable failures unless the HTTP status says otherwise.\n\

n### Sign-in challenges

Some MCP servers allow the connection and ask for sign-in only on a protected
call. The API never star

ts a sign-in. It reports the challenge instead:

* **HTTP 401 from the MCP server** on `tools/call`: the API answers
 `403 AUT
H_REQUIRED`. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge:\n its `source` (`http_401`), and the `error`, `requiredScope`,
and\n `resourceMetadataUrl` the server sent, when present.\n* **An `isError` result carrying `_meta[\"mcp/www_authenticate\"]`**
(the\n ChatGPT convention): the call succeeds, and the `CallToolResult` is returned\n unchanged with an additive `authChallenge

` field (`source:
 "tool_result_meta"`). A field the server already set under that name is never
 overwritten.

`AUTH_REQU
IRED` is not `UNAUTHORIZED`: your MCPJam key is fine, so a different\nkey will not help. Complete the OAuth flow for that server y
ourself, upload the\ntoken to one of its [accounts](#server-accounts), and call again. See\n[Mid-session sign-in](https://docs.mcp

jam.com/inspector/lazy-authentication.md).

## Rate limits

Each key gets **60 requests per minute** sustained, with bursts up

to **10**.
Exceeding it returns `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header (in
seconds):

```http theme={"theme":"css-

variables"}
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 7

{ "code": "RATE_LIMITED", "message": "API key rate limit ex

ceeded. Slow down and retry." }
```

Honor `Retry-After`, add jittered exponential backoff, and expect these limits
to be tun

ed during the preview.

Other `429`s — the per-minute brakes and daily budgets described with the
endpoints below — carry `Retr
y-After` whenever the refusal knows when it\nlifts, which is the ordinary case. Treat it as a hint that is usually there\nrather t
